# Part IV — Tuning

Finding the right numbers on a running engine: the principles, then fuel, ignition, Auto Tune, knock and logging. Read chapter 37 first.

- **[37 Tuning principles](37-principles.md)** — Tuning is describing the engine's breathing truthfully (VE), choosing the mixture you want (Target Lambda), and firing the spark as early as the engine can use without knocking — in that order, one change at a time, with a wideband and a log to tell you the truth.
- **[38 Tuning fuel](38-tuning-fuel.md)** — With the engine warm and closed loop off, hold it in each part of the VE Table, compare the wideband with the target, and correct the VE by the ratio between them — then tune starting, warm-up and throttle movement against that correct base.
- **[39 Tuning ignition](39-tuning-ignition.md)** — With the fuel right and knock detection working, bring each area of the Advance Table up towards the point where more advance stops adding torque — or, where the engine knocks first, to just short of the knock — and let the corrections handle heat and cold.
- **[40 Auto tune](40-auto-tune.md)** — Auto Tune watches the wideband while you drive, works out how wrong each VE cell is, and proposes a corrected VE table that you choose to apply — the same correction chapter 38 does by hand, done over thousands of readings.
- **[41 Knock tuning](41-knock-tuning.md)** — Let each cylinder learn what it sounds like when clean, then set the Knock Threshold just above the loudest clean running and below real knock — checking both with the Knock Scope and your ears.
- **[42 Datalogging and analysis](42-datalogging.md)** — Record what the engine did — from the studio while connected, or on the ECU's own SD card without a laptop — and read the log afterwards, because a log shows what a gauge glimpsed.
